items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: I worked for Lee Collins. He's a legend, from Louisiana. We worked for a place similar to 52nd Street... So I worked for Lee Collins.

ctx.x: And I got to Chicago, and this fellow, Tiny Parham, he was a huge man. And he played organ in the Savoy Ballroom. For the skaters, and pre-prize fights, you know, like organists play for ball games and things like that? He was the house band. He played the organ there all the time. However, he would call in for dances. So he called me and asked me, he said, "I understand you're new in the city." I said, "Yes." He says, "Would you like to have a job this weekend?" I said, "Yes." So I went to the job, expecting to…

dent passed. Then I started working around Chicago with the Tony Fambrough, Danny Williams, they were all around my age, 'round 20, 19, 20. Andrade -- I can't think of his -- Vernon Andrade I think. I have it somewhere. Back of my mind. Worked with Erskine Tate, Carroll Dickerson. I worked for Lee Collins. He's a legend, from Louisiana. We worked for a place similar to 52nd Street, on that Calumet City, right on the borderline of Indiana, in Illinois.
When you say 'similar to 52nd Street,' you mean there were a lot of clubs?
